header.running_head: Enduring Injuries and Illness when Inviting People Towards Allaah

blocks.text: Hadhrat Yazeed Taymi narrates that they were with Hadhrat Hudhayfa (RA) when someone asked him, "Had I met Rasulullaah ﷺ, I would have fought fiercely and sacrificed my life." Hadhrat Hudhayfa (RA) said, "Would you really have? I saw a time when we were with Rasulullaah ﷺ during the Battle of Ahzaab. There blew that night an extremely violent and icy wind. Rasulullaah ﷺ then announced, 'The person who will go and gather intelligence about the enemy, Allaah shall make him my companion on the Day of Qiyaamah.'" The rest of the Hadith is similar to the narration of Abdul Azeez quoted above. This narration however, quotes that Hadhrat Hudhayfa (RA) said, "When I returned to Rasulullaah ﷺ, the cold struck me as soon as I arrived and I shivered. When I informed Rasulullaah ﷺ about events, he covered me with the extra part of the shawl he was performing salaah in. I then slept until dawn. When dawn arrived, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Wake up, O sleepy head.'"[^2]

Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ announced, "Who will go and see what the enemy is doing and return (with the news)?" Rasulullaah ﷺ stipulated that the person will return and added, "I shall make du'aa to Allaah that he should be my companion in Jannah." However, no one stood up because of the intense fear, hunger and cold that everyone was suffering.[^3]
Enduring Injuries and Illness when Inviting People Towards Allaah
The Incident of Two Men from the Banu Abdul Ash'hal Tribe During the Battle of Uhud

Hadhrat Abu Saa'ib (RA) narrates that a man from the Banu Abdul Ash'hal tribe reported, "My brother and I participated in the Battle of Uhud and we both returned wounded. When Rasulullaah ﷺ's caller announced that we should march in pursuit of the enemy, I said to my brother or he said to me, 'Can we miss this opportunity to march with Rasulullaah ﷺ?' By Allaah! Although we had no transport to ride and were both heavily wounded, we went with Rasulullaah ﷺ. Since my wounds were less serious than my brother's, I carried him when he could not manage and he walked at other times. In this manner, we eventually reached the place where the other Muslims were."[^4]

Another narration states that it was Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Sahl (RA) and his brother Hadhrat Raafi bin Sahl (RA) who proceeded to Hamraa'ul Asad in a wounded condition and without transport as the one carried the other.[^5]
Haakim and Bayhaqi (Vol.9 Pg.148) as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.4 Pg.114). Abu Dawood and Ibn Asaakir have also reported the Hadith in detail as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.279).
Ibn Is'haaq reporting from Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi (RA).
